item.name: Waiter Tray Upgrade
item.howToComplete: Buy the Waiter Tray upgrade.
item.cardSummary: Waiter Tray is a small Service gain. It is one of the first upgrade purchases that feeds the Service bar.

item.name: Waiter Cart Upgrade
item.howToComplete: Buy the Waiter Cart upgrade.
item.cardSummary: Waiter Cart matches Waiter Tray as a small Service gain. Buy it after the tray if staff still cannot keep plates moving.

item.name: Card Payments Upgrade
item.howToComplete: Buy the Card Payments upgrade.
item.cardSummary: Card Payments is a mid-size Service requirement. It is an upgrade purchase, not a staffing or speed check.

item.name: Customers Seated Quickly
item.howToComplete: Seat arriving customers promptly. The official wiki does not list a time in seconds.
item.cardSummary: This Service check is about seating speed, not a named upgrade. Enough servers and a clear path to tables help more than extra decor.

item.name: Customer Orders taken Quickly
item.howToComplete: Take customer orders promptly after they sit down. The official wiki does not list a time in seconds.
item.cardSummary: Order speed is a Service-bar check. Staff who can greet and take orders without a pile-up are what this row is watching.

item.name: Food Given to Customers Quickly
item.howToComplete: Get cooked food to tables promptly. The official wiki does not list a time in seconds.
item.cardSummary: This Service check is about food reaching the table. Chefs, servers, and a short kitchen-to-seat path all support it.

item.name: Have 8 Chefs
item.howToComplete: Hire 8 chefs. That is the chef hiring cap.
item.cardSummary: The Service bar wants a full kitchen staff of 8 chefs. This is a headcount check, not a chef level check.

item.name: Have 8 Waiters
item.howToComplete: Hire 8 waiters. The Workers page calls this role Servers, with the same 8-person cap.
item.cardSummary: The Service bar wants 8 waiters. The rating table uses Waiters, while the staff menu uses Servers for the same role.

item.name: Chef Average Level is 5
item.howToComplete: Raise chefs until their average level is 5. Worker levels cap at 5.
item.cardSummary: This Service row looks at chef levels, not how many chefs you hired. Average level 5 means the kitchen staff is fully upgraded.

item.name: Server Average Level is 5
item.howToComplete: Raise servers until their average level is 5. Worker levels cap at 5.
item.cardSummary: Server average level 5 is the largest Service-bar gain. It is worth more than the chef-level row and more than any single Service upgrade.

item.name: Level 2 Kitchens Upgrade
item.howToComplete: Buy the Level 2 Kitchens upgrade.
item.cardSummary: Level 2 Kitchens is a Food-bar upgrade. It is the first kitchen-tier purchase that feeds rating.

item.name: Level 3 Kitchens Upgrade
item.howToComplete: Buy the Level 3 Kitchens upgrade.
item.cardSummary: Level 3 Kitchens matches Level 2 as a Food-bar upgrade. Level 4 Kitchens exists as an upgrade, but it is not a Food rating row.

item.name: Unlock 200 Foods
item.howToComplete: Unlock 200 food dishes. This is unlock progress, not the number of dishes currently on the menu.
item.cardSummary: Unlocking 200 foods is a Food-bar milestone. It counts dishes you have unlocked, not the 10/20/10 live-menu checks.

item.name: At least 10 Starters on Menu
item.howToComplete: Keep at least 10 starter dishes on the current menu.
item.cardSummary: The Food bar wants 10 starters available to order. Unlocked starters sitting off the menu do not count.

item.name: At least 10 Desserts on Menu
item.howToComplete: Keep at least 10 dessert dishes on the current menu.
item.cardSummary: The Food bar wants 10 desserts on the live menu. This is a course-count check, separate from unlocking 200 foods.

item.name: At least 20 Mains on Menu
item.howToComplete: Keep at least 20 main dishes on the current menu.
item.cardSummary: Twenty mains on the menu is the bigger Food course check. It is worth twice as much total rating as the starter or dessert rows.

item.name: 2 Order Counters, 6 Ovens and 6 Kitchen Counters on plot
item.howToComplete: Place 2 order counters, 6 ovens, and 6 kitchen counters on the plot.
item.cardSummary: This combined kitchen setup is the largest Food-bar gain. All three counts have to be on the plot at the same time.

item.name: Music Playing in Restaurant
item.howToComplete: Play any music in the restaurant.
item.cardSummary: Atmosphere starts with music actually playing. Owning extra genres is a separate row from having a track on.

item.name: 5 Music Genres Owned
item.howToComplete: Own 5 music genres.
item.cardSummary: This Atmosphere row counts owned music genres, not whether a track is currently playing. Two genres are already unlocked when you join.

item.name: 5 Roofs
item.howToComplete: Place 5 roof pieces on the plot.
item.cardSummary: Five roofs is a small Atmosphere build check. It is a placed-item count, not a music or art requirement.

item.name: 20 Art Items on Plot
item.howToComplete: Place 20 Art category items on the plot.
item.cardSummary: The Atmosphere bar wants 20 Art items placed. This is an Art-category count, not a general decoration total.

item.name: 15 Electronic Items on Plot
item.howToComplete: Place 15 Electronic items on the plot. Build Mode lists this category as Electronics.
item.cardSummary: Fifteen Electronic items fill another Atmosphere slot. The rating table says Electronic, and Build Mode files the same items under Electronics.

item.name: 15 Fun Items on Plot
item.howToComplete: Place 15 Fun category items on the plot.
item.cardSummary: Fifteen Fun items is another Atmosphere placement check. It is separate from Art, Outdoor, and Nature counts.

item.name: 15 Outdoor Items on Plot
item.howToComplete: Place 15 Outdoor category items on the plot.
item.cardSummary: Outdoor items are worth more Atmosphere rating than Art, Fun, or Electronic counts. Fifteen Outdoor pieces add 1.0 to the category bar.

item.name: 20 Nature Items on Plot
item.howToComplete: Place 20 Nature category items on the plot.
item.cardSummary: Twenty Nature items is the largest Atmosphere gain. If the Atmosphere bar is the leftover gap, this is the highest-value placement row.

item.name: Basic Advertising Upgrade
item.howToComplete: Buy the Basic Advertising upgrade.
item.cardSummary: Basic Advertising is a small Expansions-bar upgrade. Advertising rows sit on Expansions even though they also affect customer flow.

item.name: Print Advertising Upgrade
item.howToComplete: Buy the Print Advertising upgrade.
item.cardSummary: Print Advertising is the second small advertising row on the Expansions bar. Buy it after Basic Advertising.

item.name: Billboard Advertising Upgrade
item.howToComplete: Buy the Billboard Advertising upgrade.
item.cardSummary: Billboard Advertising is another 0.25 Expansions gain. It is one of four advertising upgrades on this bar.

item.name: Media Advertising Upgrade
item.howToComplete: Buy the Media Advertising upgrade.
item.cardSummary: Media Advertising finishes the four advertising rows. Together they add 1.0 to the Expansions category.

item.name: Purchase all Restaurant Expansions
item.howToComplete: Buy every restaurant plot expansion. The Upgrades page lists eight expansion purchases.
item.cardSummary: Buying every plot expansion is the largest Expansions-bar gain. Floor upgrades, advertising, value, and seats are separate rows.

item.name: Floor 2 Upgrade
item.howToComplete: Buy the Second Floor upgrade. Third Floor exists as an upgrade, but it is not an official rating row.
item.cardSummary: Floor 2 is a small Expansions gain. The rating table names Floor 2, which matches the Second Floor upgrade.

item.name: Restaurant Value is at least 200k
item.howToComplete: Raise restaurant value to at least 200k. The info sign shows restaurant value.
item.cardSummary: A 200k restaurant value is a large Expansions check. Value comes from what you have built and bought, not from advertising alone.

item.name: 100 Seats for Customers
item.howToComplete: Place seating for at least 100 customers.
item.cardSummary: One hundred seats is the other large Expansions progress check. Tables and chairs have to add up to that capacity.

item.name: 12 Other Types of Bathroom items on Plot
item.howToComplete: Place 12 bathroom items that are not toilets or sinks. Bathroom pieces are decorative.
item.cardSummary: Twelve extra bathroom items is one of the two biggest Hygiene gains. Toilets and sinks are counted on their own rows.

item.name: 3 Toilets on Plot
item.howToComplete: Place 3 toilets on the plot.
item.cardSummary: Three toilets match the extra-bathroom row as a 2.0 Hygiene gain. Sinks are a separate count.

item.name: 3 Sinks on Plot
item.howToComplete: Place 3 sinks on the plot.
item.cardSummary: Three sinks finish the Hygiene bar. This row is a little smaller than the toilet and extra-bathroom checks, but it is still a large total-rating gain.
